prompt:
A 58-year-old man is newly diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (left ventricular ejection fraction 30%) after presenting with exertional dyspnea. He is now euvolemic on a low dose of furosemide. Blood pressure is 122/76, heart rate 78, potassium 4.2 mmol/L, and eGFR 68 mL/min/1.73 m2. He has no contraindications to guideline-directed therapy. What is the appropriate pharmacologic management?

Provide a stepwise therapeutic management plan including medications, counseling, and follow-up.

rubric_items.text: Start an angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (sacubitril/valsartan), or an ACE inhibitor/ARB if ARNI is not feasible
Start an evidence-based beta-blocker for heart failure (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, or bisoprolol)
Start a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (spironolactone or eplerenone)
Start an SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g. dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) regardless of whether the patient has diabetes
Continue a loop diuretic titrated to maintain euvolemia
Start titratable HFrEF medications at appropriate initial doses and increase toward guideline target or maximally tolerated doses; use the standard fixed HFrEF dose for the SGLT2 inhibitor
Monitor renal function and potassium after starting RAAS/MRA therapy
Introduce the four foundational HFrEF medication classes promptly rather than waiting to maximize each drug sequentially
Counsel on daily weights, sodium moderation, and symptom monitoring
Ensure appropriate vaccinations
Refer for cardiac rehabilitation
Reassess LV function after several months of therapy to evaluate ICD/CRT candidacy
Monitor blood pressure, heart rate, volume status, and medication tolerance during titration
Review the medication list for drugs that can exacerbate heart failure
If switching from an ACE inhibitor to sacubitril/valsartan, allow at least 36 hours after the last ACE inhibitor dose
Start digoxin routinely as a substitute for foundational disease-modifying therapy
Start ivabradine before attempting titration of an evidence-based beta-blocker
Prescribe routine potassium supplementation despite a normal potassium level
Start aspirin solely because the patient has HFrEF without another indication
Start a statin solely for HFrEF without an atherosclerotic cardiovascular indication
Start a nondihydropyridine calcium channel blocker (verapamil or diltiazem) for rate control
Prescribe an NSAID for musculoskeletal complaints
Start thiazolidinedione (e.g. pioglitazone) for diabetes management
Withhold beta-blocker therapy indefinitely because ejection fraction is low
Combine an ACE inhibitor with an ARB
Withhold an SGLT2 inhibitor because the patient does not have diabetes
Use atenolol or immediate-release metoprolol in place of an evidence-based HFrEF beta-blocker
Start routine anticoagulation without atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, LV thrombus, or another indication
Delay all additional foundational therapies until the first medication reaches its target dose
Co-prescribe an ACE inhibitor together with sacubitril/valsartan (with or without an additional ARB)
Treat the HFrEF with loop diuretic monotherapy while omitting disease-modifying therapy
